context: This evaluation assesses how effectively the engineer uses the make-read-only-util package to implement a mutation tracking system. The focus is entirely on proper usage of buildMakeReadOnly, the custom logger callback, the skippedClasses parameter, and understanding of the four violation types.

checklist.name: Uses buildMakeReadOnly
checklist.description: Correctly imports and calls buildMakeReadOnly as the factory function to create the makeReadOnly tracking function. This is the core API of the package.

checklist.name: Custom logger implementation
checklist.description: Implements a custom ROViolationLogger callback function that collects violations with all four parameters (violation type, source, key, value). The logger should store violations in an array or similar structure for later retrieval.

checklist.name: Maps violation types
checklist.description: Correctly maps the four ROViolationType values (FORGET_MUTATE_IMMUT, FORGET_DELETE_PROP_IMMUT, FORGET_CHANGE_PROP_IMMUT, FORGET_ADD_PROP_IMMUT) to the spec's violation types (mutation, deletion, replacement, addition) in the reporting methods.

checklist.name: Passes skippedClasses parameter
checklist.description: Correctly passes the excludedClasses array as the second parameter (skippedClasses) to buildMakeReadOnly to enable class filtering functionality.

checklist.name: Wraps makeReadOnly appropriately
checklist.description: Uses the makeReadOnly function returned by buildMakeReadOnly in the trackObject method, passing both the object and source string. Maintains the return value to preserve referential equality.

checklist.name: Implements reporting methods
checklist.description: Provides getViolations() and getViolationSummary() methods that correctly aggregate and transform the logged violation data into the specified output formats with proper type conversions and counting.
